newsitem.title: CHINA: China widens international trade reporting system.
newsitem.headline: China widens international trade reporting system.

text.p: China has widened its international trade reporting system to include investments and securities trading by financial institutions done on their own account, the official Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.
As from Wednesday, all Chinese financial sector firms must report all their direct investments in companies overseas to the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE).
The firms must also report all transactions, including securities trading, conducted abroad, the agency quoted a SAFE statement as saying.

China established an international trade reporting system at the start of 1996 covering transactions conducted through financial institutions, but excluding business done by the institutions themselves.
The agency said the purpose of the system was to supply the central government with accurate and comprehensive statistics to allow China to merge more closely with the world economy.
